Reports

Source: vignettes/v06-reports.Rmd
v06-reports.Rmd

Documents and layout steps built documents; this vignette turns them into report files. A report is a document that is written to a file: Word (DOCX), PDF, HTML or Markdown. The file says who made it and when, it looks the same whoever opens it, and pubflow refuses to write it if it has a hole in it. This vignette goes through

  • what is added at render time and what is not part of the pipeline;
  • the report spec, which sets up a format;
  • failed steps in a report;
  • the extras of Word files: header, footer, locks and the reference document;
  • what each format needs, and the setup of PDF output.

It builds on pipeflow’s vignette Error handling for failed steps.

Requirements

pubflow calls pandoc directly, so Word and PDF need the tools that pandoc and its writers use. Which tools pub_render() needs depends on the format:

Format Needs
HTML, Markdown nothing
Word (DOCX) pandoc (>= 3.6)
PDF pandoc and xelatex (the default) or Typst

pandoc is found via the environment variable PUBFLOW_PANDOC, then RSTUDIO_PANDOC, then the PATH.

xelatex is found on the PATH by pandoc. Tables need the LaTeX packages of huxtable (huxtable::install_latex_dependencies()), and pubflow itself needs pdflscape, fancyhdr, lastpage, float and newunicodechar. With TinyTeX:

tinytex::tlmgr_install(c("pdflscape", "fancyhdr", "lastpage", "float",
                         "newunicodechar"))

Typst is found via the environment variable PUBFLOW_TYPST (the executable or its directory), then the PATH, then the typst that comes with Quarto.

The example

The document of the previous vignettes: a table and a figure of a linear model of the ozone concentration. Its header and footer lines have the token trace, which becomes the trace stamp of the report.

library(pipeflow)
library(pubflow)
library(ggplot2)

fit <- lm(Ozone ~ Temp, data = airquality)
coefs <- data.frame(term = names(coef(fit)), estimate = unname(coef(fit)))

doc <- pub_doc(
    pub_section(
        "Results",
        pub_text(sprintf(
            "The model explains **%.0f%%** of the variance.",
            100 * summary(fit)$r.squared
        )),
        pub_table(
            coefs,
            caption = "Coefficients of the linear model",
            digits = c(estimate = 3L)
        ),
        pub_figure(
            ggplot(airquality, aes(Temp, Ozone)) + geom_point(na.rm = TRUE),
            caption = "Ozone by temperature",
            width = 6,
            height = 3.5
        )
    ),
    title = "Ozone in New York",
    meta = list(
        header = c(left = "Ozone study", right = "Draft"),
        footer = c(left = "{trace}")
    )
)

Render-time metadata

Who rendered a report, when and with which application are facts about the act of rendering. They are not part of the pipeline: if they were params of the layout step, every render would outdate it. They are passed to pub_render() instead, where they are merged over the metadata of the document:

file <- pub_render(
    doc,
    "docx",
    meta = list(author = "Jane Doe", app = "ozone-app", version = "1.2.0")
)
basename(file)
# [1] "20261114T143337Z_ozone_in_new_york.docx"
  • The entries of meta win over those of the document, and NULL removes one.
  • time is the render time, unless the document or meta sets one.
  • The file name, the title block, the trace stamp, the front matter and the post-processors (below) all see the merged result.
  • pub_markdown() and pub_html(), which the viewer uses, only see the metadata of the document, so what you see in the viewer doesn’t change from one second to the next.

In an app, meta is where the user and the version go, e.g. list(author = session$user, app = "ozone-app", version = "1.2.0").

Trace stamp

pub_trace_stamp() makes the line that trace stands for. It is an error without an author, since pubflow doesn’t guess it: on a server, the system user is only the service account. Times are always UTC, with English month names:

meta <- list(
    author = "Jane Doe",
    app = "ozone-app",
    version = "1.2.0",
    time = as.POSIXct("2026-11-02 09:30:00", tz = "UTC")
)
pub_trace_stamp(meta)
# [1] "Jane Doe at 02-Nov-2026 09:30:00 UTC (ozone-app v1.2.0)"
pub_trace_stamp(meta[c("author", "time")])
# [1] "Jane Doe at 02-Nov-2026 09:30:00 UTC"
pub_trace_stamp(list(app = "ozone-app"))
# Error in `pub_trace_stamp()`:
# ! A trace stamp needs the metadata `author`.
# ℹ Pass it to `pub_render(meta = list(author = ...))`.

File names

Without file, the report goes to R’s temporary directory under the name that pub_output_filename() makes, the render time (UTC) and the title:

pub_output_filename(list(title = "Ozone in New York", time = meta$time), "docx")
# [1] "20261102T093000Z_ozone_in_new_york.docx"

Call it yourself for a download name, e.g. in the filename of a Shiny downloadHandler().

Report specs

A report spec sets up the report of one format, and pub_render() takes it as spec. Without it, pub_report_spec(format) is used: all defaults. Printing a spec shows what it uses:

pub_report_spec("docx")
# <pubflow report spec: docx>
#   reference_docx    default
#   front_matter      title block
#   toc               depth 3
#   number_sections   yes
#   page              reference document
#   figure            default
#   labels            Table, Figure
#   lock              marked items
#   error_items       refuse
#   post_process      none
#   pandoc_args       none

Every field acts in every format that can show it. A field that the format can’t use is an error, so a setting is never silently ignored:

pub_report_spec("docx", placeholder_color = "#0083c0")
# Error in `pub_report_spec()`:
# ! `placeholder_color` can't be used for docx reports, only for html and pdf.

The fields in short (?pub_report_spec has the details):

Field What it sets
reference_docx, latex_preamble, typst_template The template of DOCX, of PDF via LaTeX, of PDF via Typst
front_matter A function that returns what replaces the title block, e.g. a title page
toc, toc_depth A table of contents after the front matter, and its depth
number_sections Number the headings or not
labels The words before the caption numbers
page Paper size, orientation and margins (pub_page()) of DOCX and PDF
figure Image format and resolution of figures
placeholder_color Colour of placeholders in HTML and PDF
lock Lock tables, figures, header and footer of DOCX files
error_items Refuse or show failed steps
post_process Functions that change the finished file
pandoc_args Extra pandoc arguments

Title page, contents and page

The front matter replaces the title block. It is a function of the document (with the render-time metadata) and the format that returns what a document can hold: sections, outputs and lists of them. Its sections are not numbered, so the numbers of the body start at 1. End it with a page break to start the contents on a new page:

title_page <- function(doc, format) {
    list(
        pub_text(paste("Prepared by", doc$meta$author)),
        pub_pagebreak()
    )
}

spec <- pub_report_spec(
    "pdf",
    front_matter = title_page,
    toc_depth = 2L,
    page = pub_page("letter", margins = c(left = 3)),
    labels = list(table = "Tab.", figure = "Fig.")
)
spec
# <pubflow report spec: pdf>
#   latex_preamble    none
#   typst_template    default
#   front_matter      function
#   toc               depth 2
#   number_sections   yes
#   page              Letter portrait, margins top 2.5, bottom 2, left 3, right 2.5 cm
#   figure            default
#   labels            Tab., Fig.
#   placeholder_color default
#   error_items       refuse
#   post_process      none
#   pandoc_args       none

A document that places pub_toc() itself (what = "sections") gets no second table of contents. Lists of figures and tables (pub_toc(what = "figures")) don’t count: to have only those, set toc = FALSE in the spec.

A spec is a plain list that is checked when it is used. To have one spec for every format, write a function that builds them, so the front matter and the labels are in one place:

my_spec <- function(format) {
    pub_report_spec(
        format,
        front_matter = title_page,
        labels = list(table = "Tab.", figure = "Fig.")
    )
}
spec_docx <- my_spec("docx")

Markdown shows the effect of a spec without any tool; the table caption now starts with “Tab.”:

path <- pub_render(
    doc,
    "md",
    file = tempfile(fileext = ".md"),
    spec = my_spec("md"),
    meta = list(author = "Jane Doe")
)
grep("Tab\\.", readLines(path), value = TRUE)
# [1] "Tab. 1: Coefficients of the linear model"

Failed steps in a report

A report has no holes: pub_render() refuses a document with error items and lists the failed steps (see Documents and layout steps). Run the pipeline of a report with the default on_error = "stop", and a failed step stops it before any document exists.

For a draft, run with on_error = "continue" and let the spec show the error items instead:

pip <- pip_new("draft") |>
    pip_add("table", function() pub_table(head(airquality), caption = "Data")) |>
    pip_add("fit", function(data = airquality) lm(Ozone ~ Height, data = data)) |>
    pip_add(
        "report",
        function(table = ~ try(table), fit = ~ try(fit)) {
            pub_doc(pub_section("Results", table, fit), title = "Draft")
        }
    )
suppressWarnings(pip_run(pip, on_error = "continue", lgr = NULL))
draft <- pip[["report", "out"]]
pub_render(draft, "md", file = tempfile(fileext = ".md"))
# Error in `pub_render()`:
# ! Can't render a document with error items (failed steps):
# ✖ step 'fit' failed: object 'Height' not found
# ℹ Reports run the pipeline with `on_error = "stop"`; error items are for the viewer.
spec <- pub_report_spec("md", error_items = "show")
withCallingHandlers(
    pub_render(draft, "md", file = tempfile(fileext = ".md"), spec = spec),
    pubflow_render_warning = function(w) {
        cat("Warning:", conditionMessage(w), "\n")
        invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    }
) |>
    invisible()
# Warning: The report shows error items (failed steps):
# ✖ step 'fit' failed: object 'Height' not found

The file has an error box where the model of the failed step would be, and the warning names the failed step. Use this for drafts only.

To check a document before rendering it, e.g. to tell the user of an app why a report can’t be downloaded yet, pub_error_items() lists its error items:

vapply(pub_error_items(draft), \(x) x$message, character(1))
# [1] "object 'Height' not found"

Word files

Header, footer and locks

The Word file of the example above shows the header and footer lines of the document, with trace expanded. They go into the header and footer part of the reference document. A look into the file shows them:

docx_text <- function(file, part) {
    dir <- tempfile()
    on.exit(unlink(dir, recursive = TRUE))
    utils::unzip(file, files = paste0("word/", part), exdir = dir)
    xml <- xml2::read_xml(file.path(dir, "word", part))
    xml2::xml_text(xml2::xml_find_all(xml, "//w:t"))
}
docx_text(file, "header1.xml")
# [1] "Ozone study" ""            "Draft"
docx_text(file, "footer1.xml")
# [1] "Jane Doe at 14-Nov-2026 14:33:37 UTC (ozone-app v1.2.0)"
# [2] ""                                                       
# [3] "Page "                                                  
# [4] "1"                                                      
# [5] " / "                                                    
# [6] "1"

The footer line at the left is the trace stamp, and “Page 1 / 1” is the reference document’s own page number. A footer line at the right replaces the page number, as in PDF.

With lock = TRUE in the spec, the file also protects itself from accidental editing: tables and figures are content controls that can’t be deleted or changed, and so are the whole header and the whole footer. An item opts out with pub_set_meta(locked = FALSE). By default, only the tables and figures with pub_set_meta(locked = TRUE) are locked, and lock = FALSE locks nothing. The locks guard against slips only, since Word lets users remove a lock in the control’s properties. The report you can rely on is the PDF.

Post-processors

Two post-processors do the work above, pub_pp_docx_header_footer() and pub_pp_docx_lock(). pub_render() adds the first to every DOCX report, the second with lock = TRUE. Add them to the spec’s post_process yourself to give them arguments, e.g. other header lines than the document’s, or a different place in the order. Listing pub_pp_docx_lock() without lock = TRUE locks the header and footer, but only the tables and figures with pub_set_meta(locked = TRUE).

Your own functions have the form function(path, doc, spec). They change the finished file in place, are called in order, and a failing one stops the render, so no file is written. This one adds a note to a Markdown report:

add_note <- function(path, doc, spec) {
    writeLines(c(readLines(path), "", "<!-- checked -->"), path)
}
spec <- pub_report_spec("md", post_process = list(add_note))
path <- pub_render(doc, "md", file = tempfile(fileext = ".md"), spec = spec)
tail(readLines(path), 1L)
# [1] "<!-- checked -->"

The reference document

The look of a Word file comes from its reference document, pubflow’s own system.file("templates", "reference.docx", package = "pubflow") unless the spec says reference_docx: A4, numbered headings, and a header and footer with bookmarks for the lines. Start your own from a copy of it and change the styles and the page in Word. The document must keep

  • the styles in the table below (pandoc finds them by name; a missing one is added unformatted);
  • the bookmarks of the header and footer lines that you use: header_left, header_center, header_right, footer_left, footer_center and footer_right (the last one surrounds “Page x / N”). A line without its bookmark is an error, so a stamp is never dropped unnoticed.
Style Type Used for
Heading 1 - Heading 5 paragraph numbered section headings (the numbering belongs to the styles)
Heading 1 Unnumbered - Heading 5 Unnumbered paragraph unnumbered sections (they keep the outline level, so they appear in the table of contents)
Item Title paragraph title line above an item
Table Caption, Image Caption paragraph numbered captions (before tables, after figures)
Figure paragraph the paragraph that holds an image
Placeholder character [text]{.placeholder} spans
Error paragraph error items (failed steps)
Title, Subtitle, Author, Date paragraph pandoc’s title block

The page setup, header and footer of the reference document apply to every section, also to landscape pages. An explicit page in the spec overrides the page of the reference document.

PDF output

pub_render() takes the engine in pdf_engine:

pub_render(doc, "pdf", file = "ozone.pdf", meta = meta) # xelatex
pub_render(doc, "pdf", file = "ozone.pdf", meta = meta, pdf_engine = "typst")

To change the look of a PDF, use latex_preamble (a file that is included after pubflow’s own header, so it can load packages and change the page style) or typst_template (start from system.file("templates", "pubflow.typ", package = "pubflow")). A custom Typst template must write $header-includes$ and the title block, and take the lines of the header and footer from $header-left$ to $footer-right$.
